note: A strong programme fit and a clear commercial misfit. He matches the two starting-point criteria emphatically: 164 lb, an Army veteran three years out who trains regularly, loves the gym and has been doing kettlebells for a week and a half — about as far from deconditioned or gym-averse as the corpus gets — and his framing is pure good-to-great, 'not that I'm overweight or anything, it's just I just like looking lean', wanting to lose about five pounds and get back to Army shape. Everything commercial fails. He is 27, not currently working, living on disability, about to start as a correctional officer specifically to bring in extra money, supporting a wife and five children, with a stated ceiling of $150 a month and savings ring-fenced as family emergency funds. Neglected health is also a miss and arguably inverted: health is the area he attends to most, alongside a wife who trains with him. Read against the internal call with Kim on this same date, where the setter described letting a 23-year-old through despite doubting financial qualification because he was 'such a good fit' and expecting to route him to the cheaper tier, this call looks like the same pattern playing out — profile fit passing the screen, income fit failing on the call, and a downsell that then fails because the prospect wants the one thing the cheap tier does not include.
